item.title: NVIDIA Launches RTX Spark Platform with DLSS 5 and Nemotron 3.5 AI Model
item.description:
NVIDIA Launches RTX Spark Platform with DLSS 5 and Nemotron 3.5 AI Model

NVIDIA introduced RTX Spark, a new Windows PC platform that combines a Blackwell RTX GPU and Grace CPU for AI development, creation, and gaming in slim laptops and compact desktops.

🔧 Platform Details

  • Powered by an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and NVIDIA Grace CPU.
  • Supports up to 128 GB of unified memory.
  • Runs the full NVIDIA CUDA stack and RTX technologies, including ray tracing and DLSS 5.
  • Includes the updated NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 plugin for Unreal Engine 5.8 with official Windows on Arm (WoA) support.
  • Native ARM64 binaries allow developers to build and package UE 5.8 applications for RTX Spark systems.

🎮 DLSS 5 Features

Technology Description
Super Resolution Reconstructs frames from a lower‑resolution input to improve performance.
Ray Reconstruction Generates additional pixels to enhance ray‑traced scenes.
Dynamic Multi Frame Generation Can generate up to five additional frames per rendered frame; the multiplier adjusts automatically to maximize smoothness.
3D‑Guided Neural Rendering Supported on RTX Spark starting with NBA 2K27.
  • DLSS 5 adds a final stage to the graphics pipeline that enhances lighting and material detail while keeping the engine‑rendered frame as the foundation.
  • Avalanche Software used DLSS 5’s SDK controls to preserve artistic intent in their game.
  • The latest NVIDIA app beta adds a faster Performance Mode (Preset C) for Frame Generation with minor image‑quality trade‑offs.
  • An October model update runs 2× faster than the September version, halves GPU overhead, and reduces VRAM usage at 4K by 20% while keeping comparable visual fidelity.
  • The model will ship by default in future DLSS 5 games.

🤖 In‑Game AI with Nemotron 3.5

  • Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4 GB is now available.
  • Provides ~40 % higher average quality against the prior model on relevant benchmarks.
  • Produces up to ~80 % fewer tokens compared with peers.
  • Engineered for maximum intelligence and speed per GB of memory, enabling responsive local experiences while preserving headroom for graphics rendering and local speech models.
  • Designed to power richer, faster in‑game character interactions with strong conversational capability, autonomous multi‑turn tool use, instruction adherence, and grounding to game state.
  • Features a Conversational mode toggle for concise, speech‑ready responses.
  • Configurable reasoning lets developers enable or disable reasoning to meet latency targets.

🚀 Performance Improvements

  • On supported GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation adapts the frame‑generation multiplier as workloads change, with a 6× Multi Frame Generation producing up to five additional frames per rendered frame.
  • The October model update halves GPU overhead and cuts VRAM use at 4K by 20%.

📦 Availability

  • RTX Spark ships with the full CUDA stack, DLSS 5 support, and the updated DLSS 4.5 plugin for Unreal Engine 5.8.
  • Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4 GB runs locally on GeForce RTX and RTX Spark devices.
  • Early‑access integrations, such as NBA 2K27, already showcase DLSS 5 on RTX Spark.
  • Wider rollout to future DLSS 5 titles is planned.

#NVIDIA #DLSS5 #AIModels #Gaming #RTXSpark

Source: NVIDIA RTX Spark Powers Neural Rendering and AI Characters in Games | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark N1X processor arrives in high-end laptops
item.description:
Nvidia RTX Spark N1X processor arrives in high-end laptops

Nvidia’s RTX Spark N1X processor is finally here, and we’ve been testing a range of powerful laptops equipped with this new ‘superchip.’

🧩 Overview

Nvidia’s RTX Spark is designed as a high-performing Arm-based System on a Chip (SoC) for laptops and small desktop computers, positioning itself as a competitor to Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. The chip features many CPU cores, Nvidia RTX Blackwell graphics, and unified memory capable of running sizable local AI models.

⚙️ Key details

  • The RTX Spark is exclusively available in high-end laptops
  • All tested models feature 20 CPU cores and 6,144 GPU CUDA cores in the flagship version
  • Lower cost configurations have 18 cores and 5,120 CUDA cores
  • Unified memory ranges from 32GB to 128GB across different models
  • Pricing starts at $2,599.99 for the 18-core version and goes up to $6,999.99 for the 20-core version

🚀 Availability

The RTX Spark is currently available in several premium laptops:

  • Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra (128GB)
  • Asus ProArt P16 (both 64GB and 128GB configurations)
  • Lenovo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 (64GB)
  • HP OmniBook Ultra (32GB)

💡 Why it matters

The processor is aimed at developers, coders, and content creators who need the ability to run local AI models and utilize the latest gaming technologies like DLSS 5. Windows on Arm has improved significantly since previous generations, with native Arm apps working well and many x86 applications running through Microsoft’s Prism emulation layer.

Antonio Di Benedetto has made an RTX Spark his daily driver, running typical work and personal applications without issues. The chip handles daily tasks well but shows more variability in gaming performance.

Gaming performance

  • Black Myth: Wukong: 70fps at 3270 x 2180 with medium settings and DLSS
  • Cyberpunk 2077: 66fps with medium settings and DLSS
  • Forza Horizon 6: 57fps with medium settings and DLSS
  • Returnal: 60fps at 1440p with high settings
  • Jedi Survivor: 60fps with DLSS upscaled to 1200p and medium settings
  • Shadow of the Tomb Raider: 60fps at 1800p with highest settings

Performance varies significantly by game and settings, with some titles like Helldivers 2 and Star Wars Zero Company being more CPU-bound and showing lower frame rates.

#Nvidia #RTXSpark #AIcomputing #Armarchitecture #laptopprocessors

Source: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops

item.title: RTX Spark laptops combine Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU and unified memory for AI agents
item.description:
RTX Spark laptops combine Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU and unified memory for AI agents

Microsoft and Nvidia held a launch party for the first wave of RTX Spark laptops last week in San Francisco, where a new wave of AI PCs took center stage amid a packed crowd and a lively hands‑on area.

🔍 Overview

  • RTX Spark is a new class of Windows laptops that pairs an Arm‑based CPU with Nvidia’s Blackwell GPU and a unified‑memory architecture.
  • The design enables powerful AI models to run locally on a laptop, making the experience of setting up an AI agent quick and easy.

🧩 Architecture & Core Tech

  • The chips inside RTX Spark laptops are Arm‑based, instead of the traditional x64 architecture used by AMD and Intel.
  • Microsoft’s Prism emulator is used for apps that don’t have a native Arm version.
  • “Each core is different. How we translate x64 to that core needs to be highly optimized, and for RTX Spark we’ve done a lot of work to optimize for its microarchitecture.” – Peter Dawoud

⚙️ Features

  • Get Started experience: “When users get into Windows for the first time, they’ll see a new Get Started experience that will launch on an RTX Spark laptop that allows them to find the agent they want, get started with that agent, install it, and get to that agent in only two clicks,” says Peter Dawoud.
  • Agent installation: Agents can be installed and updated through the Windows Store, eliminating the need to track dependencies.
  • First‑party agents: Hermes, Perplexity, and OpenClaw are the first three officially supported agents at launch.
  • Unified memory: Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra can ship with up to 128 GB of unified memory, making it possible to load huge models into memory.
  • “We made incredible investments in Unified Memory Architecture to enable you to load as much as possible into the 128GB,” says Dawoud.
  • Memory optimizations cover power, performance, battery life, and allow a game to run while rendering a video in the background.
  • Memory slider: A slider in Nvidia’s Windows app lets users manually adjust how much of the unified memory is dedicated to the GPU side. This is useful on RTX Spark laptops with 24 GB or 32 GB of memory to balance more to the GPU for particular apps and games.
  • Gaming capability: While RTX Spark laptops aren’t marketed as gaming machines, they can run the latest AAA titles. Anti‑cheat support was secured as a first step for gaming on Windows on Arm.

Supported AI Agents

Agent Status at launch
Hermes Officially supported
Perplexity Officially supported
OpenClaw Officially supported

Games with Built‑in Anti‑Cheat Support

Game Anti‑cheat support
Fortnite Supported out of the box
Marvel Rivals Supported out of the box
Arc Raiders Supported out of the box
Counter‑Strike 2 Supported out of the box
Dota 2 Supported out of the box

🚀 Availability

The first wave of RTX Spark laptops was unveiled at the San Francisco launch event. Microsoft and Nvidia are continuing to work with additional anti‑cheat providers to bring more games to the platform in the future.

💡 Why it matters

  • Combining an Arm CPU, Blackwell GPU, and up to 128 GB of unified memory lets laptops load and run large AI models locally.
  • The streamlined Windows Get Started flow reduces the steps needed to find, install, and launch an AI agent to just two clicks.
  • Unified‑memory tuning and a manual slider give users flexibility to balance performance for AI workloads and gaming on the same device.

#RTXSpark #AIagents #ArmPC #UnifiedMemory

Source: How Windows is being optimized for Nvidia’s RTX Spark laptops
